questions.question: Maximum length of humerus is measured between:

explanations.a: Incorrect. The greater tubercle is not the highest point used for maximum length measurement.
explanations.b: Correct. Maximum length of the humerus is measured from the highest point on the head of the humerus to the lowest point on the trochlea using an osteometric board.
explanations.c: Incorrect. These landmarks are not used for measuring maximum length.
explanations.d: Incorrect. These landmarks do not represent the maximum anatomical length.

questions.question: Instrument used to measure maximum humerus length is:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Sliding calipers are used for smaller linear measurements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Spreading calipers are used for measuring distances between curved surfaces.
explanations.c: Correct. An osteometric board is the standard instrument for measuring the maximum length of long bones.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Measuring tapes are not suitable for precise osteometric measurements.

questions.question: Breadth of proximal epiphysis of humerus is measured between:

explanations.a: Incorrect. These landmarks do not represent the maximum proximal breadth.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The deltoid tuberosity lies on the shaft.
explanations.c: Correct. The maximum breadth of the proximal epiphysis is measured between the head and the greater tubercle.
explanations.d: Incorrect. These points are not used for proximal epiphyseal breadth.

questions.question: Best instrument for measuring proximal epiphyseal breadth is:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Measuring tapes are not sufficiently precise.
explanations.b: Correct. A sliding caliper is used to accurately measure linear breadths of bones.
explanations.c: Incorrect. An osteometric board is mainly used for measuring bone length.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A goniometer measures angles, not breadth.

questions.question: Breadth of distal epiphysis of humerus is measured between:

explanations.a: Incorrect. These are articular surfaces rather than the widest points.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The olecranon fossa is not used for this measurement.
explanations.c: Correct. Distal epiphyseal breadth is measured as the maximum distance between the medial and lateral epicondyles.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The shaft is not part of the distal epiphysis.

questions.question: Which instrument is MOST suitable for measuring distal epiphyseal breadth using points apart?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Sliding calipers are generally used when jaws can contact parallel surfaces.
explanations.b: Correct. A spreading caliper is ideal for measuring distances between projecting anatomical points such as the epicondyles.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Measuring tapes are not suitable for precise osteometric measurements.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Osteometric boards measure maximum bone length.

questions.question: Least girth of shaft of humerus is measured using:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Sliding calipers measure linear distances, not circumference.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Spreading calipers measure distances between curved points.
explanations.c: Correct. The least circumference (girth) of the shaft is measured using a measuring tape.

questions.question: Condylo-diaphysial angle is the angle between:

explanations.a: Incorrect. This describes the neck-shaft relationship.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The surgical neck is not used in this angle.
explanations.c: Correct. The condylo-diaphysial angle is formed between the longitudinal axis of the shaft and the condylar axis.
explanations.d: Incorrect. These axes define a different anatomical relationship.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Torsion is unrelated to bone length.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Curvature and torsion are different anatomical characteristics.
explanations.c: Correct. The humeral torsion angle represents the rotational twist between the proximal and distal ends of the humerus.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Torsion does not measure epiphyseal breadth.
